memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "They are corrupt and not his children; to their shame they are a warped and crooked generation. Is this the way you repay the Lord, you foolish and unwise people? Is he not your Father, your Creator, who made you and formed you?" — Deut 32:5-6 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Having praised God as the faithful, perfect Rock, Moses now turns to the sad contrast: the people's corruption. And he makes the point unmistakable — the fault lies entirely with them, not with God. The problem was never any flaw in God; it was the crookedness of the people's own hearts. Then comes a piercing question: "Is this the way you repay the Lord... Is he not your Father, your Creator, who made you and formed you?"

That question deserves to land on us too. God is our Maker. He formed us, gave us breath, and has shown us nothing but faithfulness. How do we repay Him? So often, sadly, with forgetfulness, ingratitude, and wandering hearts. Moses calls this "foolish and unwise" — and rightly so. To turn from the God who made and loves us is the height of folly.

But notice the tender word tucked into the rebuke: "Father." Even as Moses confronts the people's sin, he reminds them of the relationship. God is not merely a distant judge; He is a Father grieved by children who have turned away. The rebuke flows from wounded love.

This is exactly the heart we see in Jesus' parable of the prodigal son — a father whose child wanders, yet who longs for their return (Luke 15). The question "is this how you repay the Lord?" is not meant to crush us, but to wake us up and turn us home. If you have been repaying God's faithfulness with a wandering heart, hear the loving call of your Father. Come home.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. How have I been "repaying" God for His faithfulness to me?
2. Does remembering God as my Father and Maker change my response to Him?
3. Is there any wandering in my heart I need to bring home to Him?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, You made me, formed me, and have been endlessly faithful — yet I have often repaid You poorly. Forgive my wandering heart, and draw me home to You. Help me live as Your grateful child. Amen.
